attributes.provenance: src/game/game/player.c::PlayerProcessPowerups, run 40, attempt.SA_playerprocesspowerups-pool-literal-and-propagation-drive.20260902.v1. Baseline (b2876d6bc): target dealt lbl_80347750(f64 0.0), lbl_803477AC(f32 0.0f), lbl_803477D0(f64 100.0), lbl_803477D8(f32 100.0f), lbl_80347A40(f64 3.0) at +0x1a0..+0x1b0 in ascending pool address; ours dealt 803477D0, 803477D8, 80347A40 first (the three spelled as `f64 charge_step = lbl_803477D0;` etc.) and only then the two we spelled as literals, so the mnemonics at +0x1ac and +0x1b0 were swapped (lfd/lfs vs lfs/lfd) - the 2-mnemonic divergence the run-39 census counted. Deleting the three locals and writing 100.0 / 100.0f / 3.0 inline (values read from the retail DOL at those addresses, not guessed) made the whole five-load block byte-exact including its FPR colours f2/f3/f5/f4/f7, closed BOTH --ops clusters at once, and took real 384 -> 340 with fuzzy 99.0989 -> 99.3116 and the raw word count 187 -> 163. Commit e34c711d6.
attributes.scope: MWCC GC 1.2.5 family; any loop preheader that deals more than one invariant FP constant where our source spells some of them as extern reads of split .sdata2 labels. The value-recovery step is mandatory: read the DOL bytes, because the label carries no type or value in symbols.txt beyond its width.

falsifier: A function whose preheader deal order is unchanged after every extern-spelled invariant constant in the loop is rewritten as its literal value (counts held), or a target whose deal order is NOT ascending in pool address while its source demonstrably used literals. Re-run: python tools/gdl/fnasm.py game/game/player.c PlayerProcessPowerups 0x190:0x1b8 --diff at any commit before e34c711d6 to see the split, and at e34c711d6 or later to see the single group.
subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: When a loop's invariant floating-point constants are dealt into a block of consecutive lf[sd] loads in the loop preheader, MWCC deals the ones that are POOL LITERALS in pool-entry order, and it deals them as one group. A constant our source spells instead as a read of an `extern f32/f64 lbl_*` is NOT part of that group: it is an ordinary statement, so it is emitted at its source-statement position, which in practice means the extern-spelled loads come FIRST (they are block-top initialisers) and the literal group follows. The target, whose source spelled all of them as literals, emits one group in ascending pool address. DIAGNOSTIC: in the aligned view the preheader load block has the right instructions and the right count but a rotated ORDER, and the target's operands read as a strictly ascending run of lbl_ addresses while ours splits into 'the ones we named' then 'the ones we wrote as literals'. CURE: read the extern's VALUE out of the retail DOL and write it as a plain literal, so all of them join the one pool-ordered group. This is the mirror image of claim.law.RC_extern-fp-symbol-cannot-defeat-a-hoist-when-the-extern-is-the-pool-entry.20260901.v1: that law says symbol-FOR-literal is inert when they are the same pool object; this one says literal-FOR-symbol is NOT inert, because it moves the load between two different scheduling populations. Not to be confused with claim.law.explicit-fp-symbol-vs-literal-zero-regression.20260830.v1, which still vetoes the OTHER direction on canonical zeros.
